subject: openharness
title: Narrowing-only subagent permission clamp via strictness rank table
one_why: Total-orders the 7 permission modes and refuses any subagent override looser than the parent, closing the escalation where a model in ask-mode spawns a trust-mode child; a rank table beats per-call-site partial-order checks and is trivially testable.

subject: openharness
title: Structural bash analysis with process-wrapper stripping for permission matching
one_why: Strips timeout/nice/env-style wrappers and splits compound commands before rule matching, so 'timeout 10 rm x' hits the same deny rule as 'rm x' -- the classic prefix-evasion hole in regex deny-lists, done without a full shell parser.

subject: openharness
title: Workspace-trust gate on hooks/statusline scripts, but soft-rollout leaves it inert by default
evidence: src/harness/trust.ts:87-89 (trustSystemActive = trust file exists); enforced at src/harness/hooks.ts:555,606
one_why: Gates hostile fresh-clone .oh/config.yaml shell hooks the right way, but because the gate only activates once the user has trusted ANY directory, a brand-new user's first cloned repo still auto-runs hooks -- the compat choice trades exactly the window the gate exists for.

subject: openharness
title: oh mcp-server exposes all tools with toolPermission rules unenforced
evidence: docs/ecosystem-compat.md:24 ('toolPermissions is NOT enforced when exposing tools via stdio'); src/mcp/server-mode.ts:12-17 (wires getAllTools() with no permission gate)
one_why: Documented as intentional (use `oh remote` for less-trusted callers), but the default stdio MCP surface still turns the binary into an unpermissioned Bash/file tool server for any local process that can open the pipe.

subject: openharness
title: OS sandbox fully delegated to @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime: opt-in, Bash-only, fail-open passthrough
one_why: Reuses the same bwrap/seatbelt package behind Claude Code's sandbox instead of building one, but any init failure silently returns null and the command runs unsandboxed, Windows is a silent no-op, and PowerShell/FileEdit/WebFetch stay unwrapped -- honestly documented, yet opting in promises less than it sounds like.

subject: openharness
title: SECURITY.md states exactly what the sandbox does not cover, including the fail-open contract
evidence: SECURITY.md:29-58 ('Default: tool execution is not sandboxed... falls back to its unsandboxed path... a future revision will add requireSandbox')
one_why: Names the tool-by-tool sandbox gaps, the platform gaps, and the fail-open semantics in the same file that shows the config to fix them -- the honesty rung pi and cline sit on, and cheaper than any control.

subject: openharness
title: MicroCompact -> importance-scored drops -> LLM summarization, with a 3-failure compaction circuit breaker
one_why: Cheapest tiers run first (truncate, stub old tool results, drop lowest-scored by role/recency/decision-point score respecting pins) and LLM summarization only fires if the cheap pass misses; after 3 consecutive compression failures it stops trying and tells the user to start fresh instead of looping.

subject: openharness
title: DeferredTool wraps tools with name+description-only prompts until ToolSearch or first call
one_why: ~15 tokens per deferred tool instead of ~150 keeps a 45-tool registry affordable; schema validation still runs against the real zod schema on activation, so laziness does not weaken input checking.

subject: openharness
title: cache_control breakpoints on system blocks, rolling conversation prefix, and tool list
one_why: Marks the last message each turn so the conversation prefix stays cached and marks the final tool def so the whole tool list caches -- the cheap 90%-off discipline most subjects in this corpus lack entirely.

subject: openharness
title: Full eval harness (orchestrator, pack loader, JUnit scorer) in-repo but no CI workflow runs it
evidence: src/evals/orchestrator.ts, src/evals/scorer.ts (parseJunitXml), 8 eval test files; grep for eval across .github/workflows/ returns nothing
one_why: The scoring machinery for model-level regression detection exists and is itself unit-tested, yet CI only builds and runs unit tests -- the gap between having evals and gating on them is one workflow file, and it is the exact ceiling separating this from verification 8.

subject: openharness
title: Loop e2e driven by scripted mock providers against real tools
evidence: src/query/e2e.test.ts:1-80 (createMockProvider + real Read/Glob tools, full stream->tool->feedback cycle)
one_why: Deterministic coverage of loop semantics (turn completion, tool_call_end payloads, follow-up feeding) without API keys or nondeterminism -- the pattern that makes 1732 test cases runnable on every push across two OSes.

subject: openharness
title: MetaHarness hill-climbs its own config: benchmark, LLM-suggest change, re-run, revert if worse
evidence: src/services/MetaHarness.ts:1-30,115 (optimizes system prompt, tool selection core-vs-deferred, model router config, compression strategy, permission rules)
one_why: Agent-side harness tuning as a product feature with automatic revert on regression; no other reviewed subject runs its own harness as search space -- but with evals unwired from CI the claimed wins are unproven, so confidence med.

subject: openharness
title: Cybergotchi: a virtual pet whose needs/personality are driven by live agent session events
evidence: src/cybergotchi/events.ts:19-30, needs.ts, personality.ts, bones.ts; REPL components src/components/CybergotchiPanel.tsx
one_why: Genuinely unlike everything else in the corpus -- session telemetry (tool runs, errors) feeds a companion sprite with need states; pure gamification, but a real engagement mechanic other harnesses could copy wholesale.

subject: openharness
title: /skill-install refuses non-permissive SPDX licenses without an explicit --accept-license flag
one_why: License hygiene enforced at the install boundary of a plugin ecosystem rather than in a policy doc -- nobody else in the corpus gates skill acquisition on declared SPDX license at all.
